instructions: Entries are immutable except for changing passes from false to true after all acceptance steps have been verified.

features.description: The new repository has a minimal Rust GTK4/libadwaita application and durable agent harness.
acceptance_steps: From a clean checkout, run scripts/bootstrap.sh successfully.
Run scripts/check.sh successfully.
Run scripts/dev.sh in an X11 session and verify one compact Echo window opens.
Verify AGENTS.md, feature-list.json, and progress.md are sufficient to select the next task.

features.description: Echo is single-instance, reactivation presents the existing settings window, closing hides it, and Quit exits.
acceptance_steps: Launch Echo twice and verify there is one process and one presented settings window.
Close the window and verify the process remains running.
Launch Echo again and verify the hidden window returns.
Choose Quit and verify the process exits.

features.description: The first release refuses unsupported non-X11 sessions clearly and does not start global input backends.
acceptance_steps: Run with a non-X11 session environment and verify the window explains that this release requires X11.
Verify no shortcut grab or paste-injection backend starts in that state.
Run in X11 and verify the unsupported-session message is absent.

features.description: Typed, versioned non-secret settings persist atomically under the XDG configuration directory with documented defaults.
acceptance_steps: Run unit tests covering every default in the porting guide.
Change settings, restart Echo, and verify they reload.
Interrupt a simulated write and verify the last valid settings remain readable.
Inspect the settings file and verify it contains no API key or transcript.

features.description: The Groq API key can be saved, replaced, detected, and removed through the desktop Secret Service without exposing its value.
acceptance_steps: Save a test key and verify the UI reports that a key exists without displaying it.
Restart Echo and verify the saved status remains.
Replace and then remove the key successfully.
Inspect configuration, logs, process arguments, and environment output and verify the key is absent.
Stop the Secret Service and verify Echo shows an actionable storage error.

features.description: The X11 backend globally emits one press and one release for an unmodified F10 hold across lock states and key repeat.
acceptance_steps: Hold F10 in another application and verify Echo receives one press and one final release.
Repeat with Caps Lock and Num Lock enabled in all combinations.
Hold F10 past the keyboard repeat delay and verify recording does not release early.
Change the keyboard layout and verify the binding is re-resolved.
Force a grab conflict and verify Echo reports it without exiting.

features.description: The user can capture, validate, save, and immediately activate a custom global shortcut while retaining the old binding on failure.
acceptance_steps: Capture a non-modifier key and verify its readable name is shown and persists after restart.
Verify Escape cancels capture and bare modifiers are rejected.
Configure a shortcut with modifiers and verify press/release works globally.
Attempt a conflicting binding and verify the old shortcut still works.
Capture the ThinkPad phone-marked key and verify the actual emitted keysym can be bound.

features.description: Echo lists live microphone inputs, supports System Default, persists a selection, and falls back when a selected device disappears.
acceptance_steps: Open the input selector and verify System Default and connected microphones appear.
Select a microphone, restart Echo, and verify the selection persists.
Disconnect the selected microphone and verify Echo returns to System Default with a clear UI update.
Reconnect a microphone and verify the list refreshes without restarting.

features.description: Echo records the selected microphone and finalizes valid 16 kHz mono PCM WAV data without blocking the GTK thread.
acceptance_steps: Record from the system default and a specifically selected microphone.
Inspect each WAV and verify 16 kHz, mono, 16-bit PCM metadata.
Run conversion tests for representative mono/stereo integer and float device samples.
Interact with the settings window during recording and verify it remains responsive.
Simulate device loss and verify capture terminates cleanly with no poisoned next recording.

features.description: The Groq client prewarms and submits WAV transcription requests with the selected model, language, vocabulary, and style prompt.
acceptance_steps: Use a mock server to verify endpoint method, authorization, multipart file, model, language, prompt, and response format.
Verify auto-detect omits the language field.
Verify empty vocabulary still includes the selected style exemplar.
Verify surrounding whitespace is trimmed from returned text.
Verify connection prewarm failure does not fail the later transcription.

features.description: Groq and network failures map to short actionable errors without leaking secrets or transcript content.
acceptance_steps: Test missing key, 401/403, 413, 429, 5xx, malformed response, timeout, DNS, and offline mappings.
Verify a useful Groq error.message is shown with a bounded length.
Verify requests are not automatically retried.
Inspect captured logs and verify keys, authorization values, audio, and transcript text are absent.

features.description: The X11 backend pastes transcript text into the previously focused application using the clipboard and XTEST while preserving focus.
acceptance_steps: Paste into a GTK entry, browser field, terminal, and rich text editor.
Verify Echo never takes focus during the paste.
With a text clipboard value present, verify it is restored after paste.
Change the clipboard during paste and verify Echo does not overwrite the newer value.
Force injection failure and verify the transcript remains on the clipboard with an actionable error.

features.description: The controller implements the complete hold-to-record transaction with a 300 ms minimum, Escape cancellation, and no overlapping work.
acceptance_steps: Run controller tests for every transition and invalid event in Idle, Recording, Transcribing, and Error.
Tap the shortcut for less than 300 ms and verify no request or paste occurs.
Hold, speak, and release and verify one recording, request, and paste occur.
Press Escape while recording and verify no request or paste occurs and Escape does not reach the focused app.
Attempt another hold while transcribing and verify it is ignored.
Verify temporary audio is deleted after success, empty speech, cancellation, and every failure.

features.description: Model, language, Normal/Lower Case style, and custom vocabulary controls match the macOS Groq behavior.
acceptance_steps: Verify both required Groq model IDs can be selected and persist.
Verify Auto-detect and every required language can be selected and persist.
Verify Normal returns text unchanged and Lower Case lowercases the result.
Verify vocabulary persists and is joined with the style exemplar.
Start recording, change a setting, and verify the active transaction uses its starting snapshot.

features.description: A non-interactive X11 overlay communicates recording, transcribing, and timed error states without stealing focus.
acceptance_steps: Verify a red pulse appears near the active monitor's bottom center while recording.
Verify a faster neutral pulse appears while transcribing.
Verify a one-line error appears for 2.5 seconds and then hides.
Verify the overlay accepts neither focus nor pointer input and is absent from task switchers.
Verify focus remains in the original application across all states.
Exercise the overlay on a multi-monitor X11 setup.

features.description: Echo tracks lifetime dictated words and exposes the memory-only last successful transcript for copying.
acceptance_steps: Complete a transcription and verify its whitespace-delimited words are added once.
Restart Echo and verify the total persists and the last transcript is empty.
Copy the last transcript and verify exact clipboard text.
Verify failed, empty, short, and cancelled recordings change neither value.

features.description: The compact libadwaita settings window exposes every required setting, API-key action, status, Help, and Quit without an engine picker.
acceptance_steps: Verify every control and action specified in the porting guide is present and functional.
Verify no local/Groq engine picker, tray requirement, or out-of-scope feature appears.
Resize within reasonable bounds and verify labels and controls remain usable.
Navigate all controls with the keyboard and verify useful accessible names.
Verify the window uses Echo branding without copying macOS menu styling.

features.description: Launch at login is controlled by an XDG autostart desktop file tied to the current executable path.
acceptance_steps: Enable launch at login and inspect a valid desktop file under the XDG autostart directory.
Log into a test X11 session and verify Echo starts once.
Disable the setting and verify the autostart file is removed.
Move the binary and verify the UI warns or requires retoggling rather than silently writing an invalid path.

features.description: The complete dictation workflow passes the documented X11 manual matrix and a clean-checkout automated suite.
acceptance_steps: Run scripts/bootstrap.sh and scripts/check.sh from a clean checkout.
Record dated evidence for every manual X11 acceptance case in the porting guide.
Verify the core hold F10, speak, release, paste path repeatedly in two X11 environments.
Verify no tested exit path leaves temporary audio or a stuck key grab.
Verify no API key or transcript content appears in logs.

features.description: A versioned x86-64 tarball runs without a Rust toolchain on the documented baseline and accurately states its dynamic dependencies and X11 limitation.
acceptance_steps: Build in a clean container based on the oldest supported distribution.
Inspect the binary with ldd and document every required runtime package.
Extract the tarball on a clean matching X11 system and run Echo without a Rust toolchain.
Verify the archive contains the binary, README, license, and icons in the documented layout.
Generate and verify the published SHA-256 checksum.
Verify the README prominently says X11-only and x86-64 glibc.

features.description: A non-implemented Wayland design note validates the existing backend seams against XDG Global Shortcuts and persistent Remote Desktop portal authorization.
acceptance_steps: Document the portal session lifecycles, Activated/Deactivated mapping, restore-token rotation, and cancellation behavior.
Verify the design fits behind the existing ShortcutBackend and PasteBackend seams without changing controller behavior.
List minimum portal interface versions and a GNOME/KDE test matrix.
Verify no Wayland implementation or compositor-specific dependency was added to the X11 release.
